title: Specialization and identity restriction of the universal compact-support action
statement: For positive N, finite commutative A killed by N, supplied normalized Tate transport t, a Noetherian S with N invertible, and d≥0, the identity matrix acts as the identity on the affine trace source. Form the universal matrix action on that source over GL_d,S. For every g in GL_d(Γ(S,O)), there is an isomorphism C from its pullback along the section of g to the affine trace source over S such that pullback(universal action) followed by C equals C followed by the action of g. In particular its restriction along the identity section is the identity, by cancellation. This states specialization and normalization only, not constancy of the universal action or preservation of a trace. The objects and actions are those of [def-amb-affine-linear-universal-action].

proof.text: The identity matrix gives the identity polynomial map. Its coefficient pullback is the identity pullback comparison by the left unit law and naturality. Apply unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_baseChange_id and cancel the coordinate-tower comparison to prove affineLinearAction_one.

The coefficient tower is descended from the ordered shifted Tate tensor on the base. Build its base-change isomorphism using the tensor and shifted-line pullback isomorphisms and the Cartesian projection square. Associativity of inverse-image composition proves descended_coefficient_square; naturality then proves coefficientBaseChange_equivariant. No compatibility of arbitrary trace normalizations is required.

Apply affineLinearExchange_action_naturality to the linear-map squares and the coefficient isomorphism. Compact-support base change is invertible on the affine projections. Conjugate its equation by the coordinate-tower compact-support comparisons; this constructs the comparison C and proves action_baseChange.

Take the base-change map to be the section of g in the existing determinant-open. The universal matrix specializes to g, so action_baseChange is the stated family formula. At g=1, affineLinearAction_one and cancellation give identity restriction. Dimension zero and an empty base use the same unit equations.
